findings.title: Missing NULL check after ossl_quic_build_new_token causes segmentation fault
findings.message: The function ossl_quic_get_peer_token calls ossl_quic_build_new_token(peer, NULL, 0) to create a lookup key, but does not check if the returned key is NULL before using it in lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve(). When the peer address hasn't been set on a QUIC channel yet (as happens early in connection establishment in the http3 demo), ossl_quic_build_new_token returns NULL because BIO_ADDR_rawaddress fails on the uninitialized peer. The NULL key is then passed to lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve which dereferences it, causing a segmentation fault.
findings.suggestion: Add a NULL check for the key returned by ossl_quic_build_new_token before using it in lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve. Return 0 (failure) if key is NULL.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ossl_quic_get_peer_token function was introduced without proper error handling for the case where ossl_quic_build_new_token returns NULL. The ossl_quic_build_new_token function returns NULL when BIO_ADDR_rawaddress fails on the peer parameter, which occurs when the peer address hasn't been set on the QUIC channel yet. The code proceeds to use this NULL key in lh_QUIC_TOKEN_retrieve without checking.
